newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CALL MONEY UP A TOUCH, OTHER RATES UNCHANGED.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CALL MONEY UP A TOUCH, OTHER RATES UNCHANGED.

text.p: Dutch call money rates rose fractionally on Monday, other rates were unchanged in thin trade and dealers said prices would probably cling to current levels unless the German Bundesbank makes a move on interest rates.
Dealers said the German Bundesbank could very well raise interest rates soon after the summer recess, especially if the dollar starts climbing again.
The Bundesbank meets again on August 21.
The dollar was off its earlier peak on Monday, trading at 2.0920/25 guilders at 1120 GMT, up from 2.08 guilders in early trade, versus over 2.12 guilders last Thursday.
Call money rates were bid at 3.18 to 3.25 percent versus some 3.12 percent on Friday.
One-month deposits were glued to Friday's 3.30 percent bid and three-month deposits were unchanged at 3.34 percent bid.
The guilder was a touch stronger versus the mark at 112.660 per 100 marks from 112.675 on Friday.
